notes: PRIME sponsor (seq 0 of 14) of RS2025-1101, requesting Finance and the Planning Housing Division to determine the feasibility of a special revolving loan fund for affordable housing capitalized by community, business and nonprofit lenders, and recommend the vehicle (Metro fund, the Nashville Housing Catalyst Fund, or a new public-private partnership). Also sponsor (seq 4 of 6) of RS2025-1616, dedicating a portion of the state real estate transfer tax to affordable housing and senior home repair. Every instrument she names is targeted public FINANCING - loan funds, the Barnes Fund, the Housing Catalyst Fund. Chair 2 is excluded: no rent cap and no inclusionary requirement appears anywhere in either text. Chairs 4 and 5 are excluded outright by proposing government action at all.

Sponsor (seq 4 of 6) of RS2025-1616, urging the Tennessee General Assembly to authorize county impact fees and dedicate part of the real estate transfer tax to local infrastructure, against a documented $15.5 billion Davidson County infrastructure gap that property tax revenue cannot meet. The text argues explicitly that "modest, well-calibrated fees can generate revenue without discouraging development" - i.e. fund infrastructure to support growth rather than slow it. That excludes chair 2 (slow approvals until capacity catches up) from her own words, and excludes chair 4 in the opposite direction, which would REDUCE fees.

Sponsor (seq 2 of 33) of BL2026-1391, the enacted Title 17 zoning text amendment admitting data centers as a use subject to conditions: written utility confirmation of adequate water and sewer capacity, with NO zoning permit if capacity is insufficient; a required noise impact assessment measured at 500 feet; a 2,640-foot separation from residential, daycare, religious, park and school uses; EPA Tier 4 generator emission standards with enclosed sound attenuation and testing logs; at least 10-15 percent of total power from renewable sources additive to TVA; and a decommissioning and R2-certified recycling plan. Campus scale (over 500,000 sq ft or 100MW) is barred from Davidson County entirely. That is admission subject to impact assessment and conditions before approval, not a moratorium (chair 1) and not streamlined permitting (chair 4).

Sponsor (seq 6 of 9) of RS2025-1711, urging the Office of Homeless Services to use the $4.4 million FY26 appropriation (BL2025-833) on Permanent Supportive Housing and Rapid Rehousing so that no Nashvillian loses permanent housing to HUD's expected shift of Continuum of Care priorities away from permanent supportive housing toward temporary interventions, capping permanent housing at 30 percent when Nashville spends well above that. Defending permanent supportive housing as the strategy against a shift to temporary shelter is exactly the chair 1 / chair 2 distinction, decided here for chair 1. NOTE the limit: chair 1's other clauses - no preconditions, avoid criminalization entirely - are not evidenced by this text, which is silent on enforcement.
